chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Hafs al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the child is born, an Aqeeqa sacrifice is performed for him, his head is shaved, charity is given equal to the weight of his hair, the leg along with the thigh is gifted to the midwife, a group of Muslims are invited to eat and supplicate for the boy, and he is named on the seventh day.

key_terms.عُقَّ: Aqeeqa, the sacrifice of an animal on the occasion of a child's birth

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals and obligations for a newborn child in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the comprehensive ritual framework for welcoming a newborn, linking the Aqeeqa sacrifice and head-shaving to the prophetic tradition of expressing gratitude through charity proportional to the hair's weight. It further emphasizes communal celebration by inviting guests and naming the child on the seventh day, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a means of integrating the child into the Muslim community.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Hafs Al Kunasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The child, when it is born, perform Aqeeqa for him, and shave off his head, give in charity by the weight of the hair, and gift to the mid-wife, the leg (of the sacrificed animal) along with the leaf (silver or gold), and invite a number from the Muslims, so they should be earring and supplicating for the boy, and name him on the seventh day’.
en.sarwar: 12. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban from Hafs al-Kunasiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘When ‘Aqiqah is offered for a child, his head is shaved, equal to the weight of his hair charity is given, one leg and hip is given to al-Qabilah (the special nurse, doctor), Muslims should be invited and when they are served they should pray for the boy. A name can be given to the child on the seventh day of his birth.’”
